spots.name: St Machar's Cathedral
spots.summary: St Machar's Cathedral is a Church of Scotland church in Aberdeen, Scotland, located to the north of the city centre, in the former burgh of Old Aberdeen. Technically, St Machar's is no longer a cathedral but rather a high kirk, as it has not been the seat of a bishop since 1690.

spots.name: Marischal College
spots.summary: Marischal College was one of the two universities in Aberdeen between 1593 and 1860, alongside King's College, Aberdeen, with which it merged to form the University of Aberdeen in 1860.

names.ja: マーシャル・カレッジ

spots.name: Aberdeen railway station
spots.summary: Aberdeen railway station serves the city of Aberdeen in north east Scotland. It is the busiest railway station in Scotland north of the major cities of Edinburgh and Glasgow. It is located on Guild Street in the city centre, adjacent to Union Square.

spots.name: Kirk of St Nicholas
spots.summary: The Kirk of St Nicholas is a historic church in Aberdeen, Scotland. It is the original parish church of the city, and is also known locally as the Mither Kirk or mother church. Following the Reformation, it was divided between two congregations, the East Kirk and the West Kirk.

names.ja: セイント・ニコラス、アバディーン

spots.name: Aberdeen Art Gallery
spots.summary: Aberdeen Art Gallery is the main visual arts exhibition space in the city of Aberdeen, Scotland. It was founded in 1884 in a building designed by Alexander Marshall Mackenzie, with a sculpture court added in 1905. In 1900, it received the art collection of Alexander Macdonald, a local granite merchant.

photo.author: Tom Parnell from Scottish Borders, Scotland

spots.name: St Andrew's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Andrew's Cathedral, or the Cathedral Church of Saint Andrew, is a cathedral of the Scottish Episcopal Church situated in the Scottish city of Aberdeen. It is the see of the Bishop of Aberdeen and Orkney, who is the Ordinary of the Diocese of Aberdeen and Orkney.

spots.name: St Mary's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of St Mary of the Assumption, usually known as St Mary's Cathedral, is a cathedral of the Roman Catholic Church in the city of Aberdeen, Scotland.

names.es: Catedral de Nuestra Señora de la Asunción de Aberdeen

spots.name: Union Street
spots.summary: Union Street is a major street and shopping thoroughfare in Aberdeen, Scotland. It is named after the Acts of Union 1800 with Ireland.

spots.name: Provost Skene's House
spots.summary: Provost Skene's House is a house in Aberdeen, built in 1545 and now housing a museum. It is named after Sir George Skene (1619–1708) who served as provost of the city of Aberdeen from 1676 to 1685. Skene bought the house in 1669 and is thought to have commissioned its 17th-century plaster ceilings.

spots.name: Union Terrace Gardens
spots.summary: Union Terrace Gardens is a public park and gardens situated on Union Terrace in Aberdeen, Scotland.

spots.name: Tolbooth Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Tolbooth in Aberdeen, Scotland is a 17th-century former jail which is now operated as a museum. The museum contains prison cells and exhibits various police and law and order related items. The building has been featured on popular television as the setting for a ghostlore story.

spots.name: Aberdeen Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aberdeen Castle was a late Middle Ages fortification, in Aberdeen, Scotland. It was situated on Castle Hill, a site today known as the Castlegate, and the location of the castle is now occupied by blocks of flats.

spots.name: Robert Gordon's College
spots.summary: Robert Gordon's College is a co-educational private school for day pupils in Aberdeen, Scotland. The school caters for pupils from nursery through to S6.

names.ja: ロバート・ゴードンズ・カレッジ

spots.name: Statue of William Wallace, Aberdeen
spots.summary: The William Wallace Statue was erected 1888 in Aberdeen, Scotland, and depicts Sir William Wallace. Sculpted by William Grant Stevenson, the statue is positioned opposite His Majesty's Theatre and across from Union Terrace Gardens.

spots.name: Brig o' Balgownie
spots.summary: The Brig o' Balgownie is a 13th-century bridge spanning the River Don in Old Aberdeen, Scotland. It is the oldest standing bridge in Scotland.

spots.name: Triple Kirks

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Triple Kirks in Aberdeen, Scotland were built at the time of the Disruption of 1843 when the Free Church of Scotland split from the Church of Scotland. The three churches were all part of a single building with a tall spire but they housed separate congregations.

spots.name: His Majesty's Theatre
spots.summary: His Majesty's Theatre is a theatre in Aberdeen, Scotland, and the largest in north-east Scotland, seating more than 1,400. It stands on Rosemount Viaduct, opposite the city's Union Terrace Gardens, and was designed by Frank Matcham and opened in 1906.

names.ja: ヒズ・マジェスティーズ・シアター

spots.name: Aberdeen Maritime Museum
spots.summary: Aberdeen Maritime Museum is a maritime museum in Aberdeen, Scotland, located on the historic Shiprow near the city harbour.

spots.name: Greyfriars Church, Aberdeen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Greyfriars Church is a Category A Listed building in Aberdeen, Scotland. It was designed by the architect Alexander Marshall Mackenzie and built in 1903. It is situated on Broad Street and forms the south-east corner of Marischal College, also designed by Mackenzie.

spots.name: King's College Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: King's College Chapel is the chapel of King's College in the University of Aberdeen. The chapel's Crown Tower is considered one of the most recognisable symbols of both the university and Aberdeen.

spots.name: Aberdeen Grammar School
spots.summary: Aberdeen Grammar School is a state secondary school in Aberdeen, Scotland. It is one of thirteen secondary schools run by the Aberdeen City Council educational department.

names.ja: アバディーン・グラマースクール

photo.author: The original uploader was Jimmyjojojr at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Duthie Park
spots.summary: Duthie Park is a public park in the Ferryhill area of Aberdeen, Scotland located near the River Dee. It comprises 44 acres (180,000 m2) of land given to the council in 1881 by Elizabeth Crombie Duthie of Ruthrieston, in memory of her uncle and of her brother.

photo.author: The original uploader was PMJ at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Girdle Ness Lighthouse
spots.summary: Girdle Ness Lighthouse is situated near Torry Battery on the Girdle Ness peninsula just south of the entrance to Aberdeen's harbour, in Scotland. It is an active light, managed by the Northern Lighthouse Board.

spots.name: Rubislaw quarry
spots.summary: Rubislaw Quarry is a quarry situated at the Hill of Rubislaw in the west end of the city of Aberdeen, Scotland.

spots.name: Aberdeen's Mercat Cross
spots.summary: Aberdeen's Mercat Cross was built in 1686 by John Montgomery, an Aberdeen architect. It is in the Castlegate area in the old burgh of New Aberdeen.

spots.name: Union Bridge, Aberdeen
spots.summary: Union Bridge is a bridge on Union Street in Aberdeen, Scotland. It is the largest single-span granite bridge in the world, at 130 feet. It was built by Thomas Fletcher under some influence from Thomas Telford. It is a Category B listed building with Historic Scotland.

spots.name: Belmont Street
spots.summary: Belmont Street is a north-south street in the centre of Aberdeen, Scotland that runs perpendicular to Union Street.

photo.author: The original uploader was Bobbacon at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Marischal Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Marischal Museum was a museum in Aberdeen, Scotland, specialising in anthropology and artifacts from cultures around the world.

spots.name: Bridge of Dee
spots.summary: The Bridge of Dee or Brig o Dee is a road bridge over the River Dee in Aberdeen, Scotland. The term is also used for the surrounding area of the city. Dating from 1527, the bridge crosses at what was once the City of Aberdeen's southern boundary.

spots.name: St Peter's Church, Aberdeen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Peter's Church is a Roman Catholic Parish church in Aberdeen, Scotland. It was built from 1803 and opened in 1804. It is situated on Justice Street between Peacock's Close and Market Stance, next to St Andrew's Cathedral in the centre of the city.

spots.name: King Street
spots.summary: King Street is one of the main streets in the city of Aberdeen, Scotland.

spots.name: Torry Battery
spots.summary: The Torry Battery is an artillery battery near Torry in Aberdeen, Scotland, which has overlooked the city's harbour since 1860. It was originally constructed for nine guns with a defensible barracks at the rear. In 1881 the battery mounted three 10-inch Smooth bore guns and five 68-Pounder Smooth bore guns.

spots.name: Broad Street
spots.summary: Broad Street is a street in Aberdeen which joins Union Street in the southeast and the Gallowgate and Upperkirkgate in the northwest.

spots.name: Aberdeen Sheriff Court Annex and High Court of Justiciary
spots.summary: The Aberdeen Sheriff Court Annex and High Court of Justiciary, also known as Mercatgate, is a judicial building in Castle Street, Aberdeen, Scotland.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Aberdeen Sheriff Court Annex and High Court of Justiciary

spots.name: Seaton Park
spots.summary: Seaton Park is a public park in the Old Aberdeen area of Aberdeen, Scotland. One of the city's biggest parks, it was bought by the city for use as a public park in 1947 from Major Malcolm Vivian Hay, a cryptographer during the First World War and a historian of Catholic and Jewish history.

spots.name: Pittodrie Stadium
spots.summary: Pittodrie Stadium, commonly referred to as Pittodrie, from which the surrounding residential area has taken its name, is an all-seater stadium in Aberdeen, Scotland. Used primarily for football, it has been the home ground of the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) club Aberdeen F.C.

names.ja: ピットドリー・スタジアム

spots.name: Bon Accord Baths
spots.summary: Bon Accord Baths, previously the Uptown Baths, is a category B listed Art Deco indoor swimming pool and baths complex in Aberdeen, Scotland. It is recognized as one of the most significant surviving indoor swimming pools of the interwar period in the UK.

spots.name: Wellington Suspension Bridge
spots.summary: The Wellington Suspension Bridge is a suspension bridge crossing the River Dee from Ferryhill to Craiglug in Aberdeen, north east Scotland. Designed by Captain Samuel Brown and the Aberdeen City Architect John Smith, it was opened to pedestrians in November 1830 and to traffic in May 1831.

spots.name: Gordon Highlanders Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Gordon Highlanders Museum is based in Aberdeen, Scotland and celebrates the story of the Gordon Highlanders regiment, which originated as the 92nd Regiment of Foot in 1794, merged with the 75th (Stirlingshire) Regiment of Foot to form the Gordon Highlanders in 1881 and was then amalgamated into a new larger unit of the British Army in 1994.

spots.name: Guild Street
spots.summary: Guild Street is a main street in the city centre of Aberdeen, Scotland, close to the harbour.

spots.name: Aberdeen Beach and Queens Links
spots.summary: Aberdeen Beach and Queens Links is a coastal area in Aberdeen, Scotland, comprising a sandy beach and the adjacent public park known as Queens Links. The beach extends in a broad curve between Aberdeen Harbour and the mouth of the River Don.

spots.name: Aberdeen Arts Centre
spots.summary: Aberdeen Arts Centre is a theatre and arts centre on King Street in Aberdeen, Scotland with a 350-seater auditorium. It is a Category A listed building.

spots.name: Aberdeen Mosque and Islamic Centre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Aberdeen Mosque and Islamic Centre (AMIC) is a Sunni mosque, located in Aberdeen, Scotland, in the United Kingdom. It is the largest mosque and Islamic centre in the North East of Scotland, and operates two sites within Aberdeen.

spots.name: Tivoli Theatre, Aberdeen
spots.summary: The Tivoli Theatre is a theatre in Aberdeen, Scotland, opened in 1872 as Her Majesty's Theatre and was built by the Aberdeen Theatre and Opera House Company Ltd, under architects James Matthews of Aberdeen and Charles J. Phipps, a London-based architect brought in to consult.

spots.name: Central Library

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Central Library is the principal public library for the city of Aberdeen, Scotland. It opened in 1892 and is operated by Aberdeen City Council as part of the Aberdeen City Libraries network.

spots.name: Union Terrace
spots.summary: Union Terrace is a single carriageway street in the city centre of Aberdeen. At the south end, it has a junction with Union Street, at Union Bridge and Bridge Street; and at the north end, it has a junction with Rosemount Viaduct, with the Central Library and His Majesty's Theatre on that street.

spots.name: Cruickshank Botanic Garden
spots.summary: The Cruickshank Botanic Garden is a botanical garden in Aberdeen, Scotland. It includes a Herbarium, and houses rare and endangered plants.

spots.name: Old Town House, Old Aberdeen
spots.summary: The Old Town House is a municipal building in the High Street in Old Aberdeen, Scotland. The structure, which is now the home of the King's Museum, is a Category A listed building.

spots.name: King's Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: King's Museum was a small university museum operated by the University of Aberdeen and located in the Old Town House in Old Aberdeen, Scotland.

spots.name: Gilcomston Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Gilcomston Church is an evangelical congregation, a member of the Didasko fellowship, which meets in the church buildings on Union Street, Aberdeen. It was built in a 19th-century ecclesiastical architecture style. The congregation was formerly part of the Church of Scotland and known as Gilcomston South Church.

spots.name: Sir Duncan Rice Library
spots.summary: The Sir Duncan Rice Library is the main academic library for the University of Aberdeen. It was designed by Schmidt Hammer Lassen Architects and completed in 2011. It is named after Duncan Rice, a previous Principal of the university.

names.ja: サー・ダンカン・ライス図書館

spots.name: The Academy Shopping Centre
spots.summary: The Academy Aberdeen, previously known as "The Academy Shopping Centre", is located on the corner of Belmont Street and Schoolhill in the main shopping district of Aberdeen, Scotland. As the name suggests, it is a former Victorian secondary school renovated into a modern shopping centre.

spots.name: Johnston Gardens
spots.summary: Johnston Gardens is a small public garden in Aberdeen, Scotland. The garden has won the Britain in Bloom competition many times.

spots.name: Snow Kirk
spots.summary: The Snow Kirk in Old Aberdeen was a small but important church in Scottish history. It is now ruinous but its site remains as a small graveyard within the bounds of Aberdeen University.

spots.name: Hazlehead Park
spots.summary: Hazlehead Park is a public park in the Hazlehead area of Aberdeen, Scotland. 180 hectares in size, it was opened to the public in 1920, having formerly been the estate of Hazlehead House, home of William Rose, shipbuilder. It is heavily wooded and contains many walking tracks.

spots.name: Beach Ballroom
spots.summary: The Beach Ballroom is an art deco building on the beach boulevard of Aberdeen, Scotland. It was built in 1926 and opened on 3 May 1929. It is a Category B listed building and has been noted for its dance floor which is supported by 1,400 steel springs.

spots.name: Queen's Cross Church, Aberdeen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Queen's Cross Church is a congregation of the Church of Scotland. It is located at the intersection of Carden Place and Albyn Place, at Queen's Cross in the heart of Aberdeen's west end business community. It is a short walk from the main shopping areas of the city and several main hotels.

spots.name: Bridge of Don
spots.summary: Bridge of Don is a five-arch bridge of granite, built between 1827 and 1830, crossing the River Don just above its mouth in Aberdeen, Scotland.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Margaret of Scotland, also known as St Margaret's, Gallowgate, is a Scottish Episcopal Church, in Aberdeen, Scotland.

spots.name: King George VI Bridge
spots.summary: The King George VI Bridge is a bridge over the River Dee in Aberdeen, Scotland.

spots.name: Zoology Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This museum is on the ground floor of the university's Zoology Dept. It has a big collection of specimens, from protozoa to the great whales. Exhibits include taxidermy, skeletons, skins, fluid-preserved specimens and models.

spots.name: Prince of Wales
spots.summary: Long, long bar, almost as long as HRH Charlie's tenure of the post of Prince of Wales. It's a Belhaven pub where you need to bring an appetite for their hearty trad food. It's hidden away in a block north side of Union St, surrounded by banks that haven't yet been converted to pubs but are presumably looking anxiously over their shoulders.

spots.name: The Archibald Simpson
spots.summary: This is in a converted bank at the city's old crossroads. The historical name tells you it's a JD Wetherspoon. Simpson (1790-1847) was the architect most responsible for the granite cityscape. Reliable chain pub for real ale and food.

spots.name: Old School House

spots.summary: Belhaven pub behind a granite portico, suggesting that the former school specialised in Latin, Greek and physical chastisement. Good selection of food, TV sport, beer garden and dog friendly.

spots.summary: A tiki dive bar and Grassroots music venue. Great range of world beers, real ale and cider, authentic absinthe, rum, and outlandish tiki cocktails served in pint jars.
